summary: /edit shows the editor to anyone: signed out, you get an empty file list instead of the login page
detail: main.ts:15 serves the /edit HTML import with no auth check. The client's first fetch, /edit/pages/, is redirected to /login?next=%2Fedit%2Fpages%2F; fetch follows it, res.ok is true on the login HTML, res.json() throws, and Browser.tsx:17 swallows the error. store.ts loadFile has the same blind spot (with ?path= it would load the login page's HTML into the editor), as does ImageBrowser.tsx. The next it carries is the API path, not /edit. Already in HEAD. Fix shape: requireAuth answers fetch requests (no text/html in Accept) with 401, and one shared client fetch sends the page to /login?next=<current URL> on a 401; server.test.ts:112 pins today's 302 for API calls. First check whether Bun 1.4 lets a handler guard an HTML import directly, which would be simpler.
note: 19 Sep 2026: requireAuth answers fetches with 401 and still redirects page loads (Accept: text/html); server/edit/api.ts wraps every editor fetch and sends the page to /login?next=<path+search> on a 401. /edit stays an unguarded HTML import (a handler can't serve an HTMLBundle; it only exposes index and files), so the editor's first request does the redirect and the empty shell shows for a moment first. The 302 test became two: 401 for a fetch, 302 with next for a page load. In the pane, signed-out /edit?path=index.md landed on /login with next=/edit?path=index.md.

summary: The uncommitted 0.0.2 sandbox starves both previews: no site.css, no -theme.css, no images
detail: Preview.tsx:55 and CssPreview.tsx:37 gained sandbox="allow-scripts". Without allow-same-origin the srcdoc document's origin is null, and in the preview pane's browser every subresource it asks for fails, public or not: /static/site.css, /edit/pages/-theme.css (which would also lose the SameSite=Lax cookie) and /static/images/*. So the markdown preview renders in Times with no theme and broken images, and the CSS preview loses site.css and its sample logo (the CSS being edited is inlined, so that part still shows). Fix shape, tested: sandbox="allow-same-origin" alone. Scripts still cannot run, which is the point of the 0.0.2 fix; the frame shares the editor's origin again, so both stylesheets, the cookie and images load. Then drop the now-inert onerror="this.remove()" at Preview.tsx:45 (a missing theme is just a failed <link>) and reword CHANGELOG.md:10. Never allow-scripts together with allow-same-origin: the frame could lift its own sandbox.
note: 19 Sep 2026: fixed as tested: sandbox="allow-same-origin" on both iframes, the inert onerror removed, the CHANGELOG entry rewritten. In the demo the preview rendered with site.css and loaded /static/images/logo.svg.

summary: The server needs a pid file
detail: Asked for by Peter, 19 Sep 2026. Purpose to confirm (stopping a stray dev server, or a process manager in production?): it decides the default path and whether a pid file naming a live process (process.kill(pid, 0)) should stop a second server starting. Shape: write process.pid at startup and remove it on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM; path from an env var in config.ts; the code in its own module, since main.ts is resources and routes only. Care points: bun --hot re-runs main.ts in the same process on every reload, so exit handlers must be registered once per process, not once per reload; bun test loads .env (checked) and server.test.ts spawns its server with the runner's env, so the test server must not overwrite or delete the dev server's pid file; gitignore the file.
note: 19 Sep 2026: purpose never confirmed, so built as both a handle and a lock. server/pid.ts writes ./duckdown.pid before listening (DUCKDOWN_PID moves it, empty turns it off), refuses to start if it names another live process, and removes it on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM (registered once per process for --hot). *.pid is gitignored; tests give each server its own pid file and cover write, refusal and removal. Proved in use the same day: the desktop app reported the preview server stopped while bun run dev and the server still held :8080; kill $(cat duckdown.pid) stopped it, the file went and the port freed.

Options: point dev at a gitignored working copy seeded from tests/example (as create/setup.ts seeds ./site for a new site); or keep it and check git status before committing.

summary: The editor's file list is empty: railroad 0.11's keyed list() hands each row a Signal, and Browser.tsx reads it as a plain item
detail: Found 19 Sep 2026 demoing the editor, signed in: /edit/pages/ answers 200 with index.md, -theme.css and guide/, yet the list shows no rows. In 0.11.0's keyed form list(items, keyFn, render), render receives ReadonlySignal<T> (node_modules/@blueshed/railroad/jsx.ts, the list() overloads), so f.name is undefined and f.name.endsWith(...) throws. After its first render list() re-syncs synchronously inside files.set(), so the throw lands in load()'s bare catch {}: no console error, and folders.set() never runs. ImageBrowser.tsx has the same keyed rows (f.name; f.path in the thumbnail src and onclick), so expect rows there with no names and a src of /edit/browseundefined (not yet seen). New in the uncommitted 0.0.2 upgrade from 0.1.1; the server tests can't see it. Fix shape: read the row signal in each keyed render (f$.peek() in handlers, f$.map(...) for text), or use the index-based list(items, (f) => ...) form; and stop the empty catch hiding render errors. While it's broken, hasTheme is never set (it comes after the throwing files.set), so New offers Theme even where a -theme.css exists (seen at the root, 19 Sep 2026); choosing it overwrites that file (todo 8).
note: 19 Sep 2026: Browser.tsx and ImageBrowser.tsx read rows with f$.map(...) and f$.peek(); both load()s moved the signal updates out of the try, so a render error now surfaces (one did, from a half-edited hot reload). In the pane: the list shows guide, -theme.css and index.md; New offers no Theme where one exists; the image sidebar shows names and loaded thumbnails.

summary: New overwrites an existing file without asking: a page named after an existing one replaces it with a stub
detail: Browser.tsx onCreate (line 25) hands every choice to store.ts createFile (line 27), which PUTs a template (title: <name>, or the -theme.css stub) straight to /edit/pages/<path>, and the PUT in pages.ts writes whatever it gets. Nothing checks for an existing file, so New > Page 'index' at the root replaces index.md, and New > Theme where a -theme.css exists (offered while todo 7 is open) replaces the theme. From reading the code, not reproduced: reproducing it destroys the file. Fix shape: createFile checks the name against the listing the browser already holds and refuses (or asks); belt and braces, a create-only PUT on the server, e.g. If-None-Match: * answered with 412 when the file exists.
note: 19 Sep 2026: PUT /edit/pages/* with If-None-Match: * answers 412 when the file exists; createFile sends it and the New dialog shows '<path> already exists' and stays open. Tests cover the 412 and the create. In the demo a second New > Folder 'hello' showed 'hello/index.md already exists' and the saved page was untouched.

summary: Save flashes 'Saved' even when the save failed
detail: From reading the code 19 Sep 2026: Editor.tsx save() awaits saveFile() and then always clears dirty and flashes 'Saved'; saveFile() ignores the PUT's status, and a network error rejects past both. A 500 or a dropped connection therefore reads as saved, and closing the tab loses the work (a 401 now goes to login via api.ts). Fix shape: saveFile returns whether res.ok (false on a throw); save() keeps dirty and flashes 'Not saved' (button.danger) when it didn't.
note: 19 Sep 2026: saveFile and deleteFile return whether they worked. A failed save keeps the edit dirty and flashes 'Not saved' (button.danger) while the notice gives the reason; a failed delete leaves the file open. Covered in editor.test.tsx (a 507 staged with intercept()).

summary: Logout is a GET, so any page on the site can sign an editor out

Editors write the pages, so the harm is small; a cross-site page probably can't do it (Chrome won't let a cross-site subresource response set the Lax cookie), not tested. Fix shape: POST-only /logout; the header's Logout link becomes a small form button.
note: 19 Sep 2026: /logout is POST-only ({ POST: handleLogout } in main.ts) and refuses Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site with 403 (Sec-Fetch-Site rather than an Origin/Host comparison, which a proxy rewriting Host would break). The header's Logout is a form styled like the links beside it. Tests: POST clears the cookie, cross-site is refused, GET signs nobody out.

summary: Published pages mangle $ sequences: '$$5' shows as '$5', and '$&' pastes in the template's {{content}}
detail: Found 19 Sep 2026. site.ts:29-33 fills the template with String.replace(pattern, string), and a replacement string reads $$, $&, $` and $' as patterns. So LaTeX-style $$...$$, prices written $$, and any page that shows regex replacement syntax come out wrong on the site, while the editor's preview (built as a template literal) shows them right: what you preview is not what gets published. Checked with renderMarkdown + the same replace: 'Costs $$5. In a regex, `$&` is the match.' published as 'Costs $5 ... {{content}}amp;'. Fix: replacer functions, .replace("{{content}}", () => content), on all five; a site test with a $$ page.
note: 19 Sep 2026: all five template fields are filled with replacer functions. server.test.ts publishes a page titled '$$ and $& and $'' with 'Costs $$5' and '$&' in code, and checks they come out as written.

summary: Every page view walks the whole pages tree for the nav
detail: Noted 19 Sep 2026 (review). buildNav lists every folder and reads every index.md on each request: fine on local disk for a small site, slow and chatty on S3. Options to decide with Peter: cache the nav and drop it on the editor's writes (pages PUT/DELETE), with a short TTL for changes made outside the editor (none in development); or feature.md's 'duckie publish' to static files, which removes the per-request cost altogether.
note: 19 Sep 2026: Peter chose the cache ('since the server is responsible for writing, a nav cache is fine'). server/nav.ts: siteNav() builds once and keeps it; the pages route's PUT and DELETE call navChanged(); a failed build isn't kept. No TTL: a file changed on disk behind the server's back shows after the next editor save or a restart (said in CLAUDE.md, with the rule that any new write path must call navChanged()). Tested: a folder written straight to disk stays out of the nav until an editor write, then both appear; the unit test counts list() calls.

summary: Maths ($x^2$, $$ blocks): needs a renderer, so a decision

summary: The duckdown authoring skill was out of date, and wrong in places
detail: Peter asked 19 Sep 2026. Written 20 Mar: it taught plaintext passwords in users.json (hashes since 0.0.2), themes per folder only (they cascade), hard-coded theme colours (variables now), {{title}} defaulting to "duckdown" (it's "duckie"), click-to-copy images (it's select, then Copy Markdown); it knew nothing of toc, callouts, wiki links, heading links, dark mode, the nav marks, New's no-overwrite, or the nav cache; and its name (duckdown-authoring) didn't match its folder.
note: 19 Sep 2026: rewritten as a lean SKILL.md (where the content lives, writing a page, the six traps, how to check) plus reference.md with a contents list (content folder, pages and URLs, front matter, markdown, navigation, themes and every variable, template, static files and images, users, the editor, troubleshooting), following the skill-creator's pattern and railroad's bun-route. name: duckdown; a fuller, more assertive description. Claims checked against the code. CLAUDE.md now says to update the skill and the guide pages whenever a content feature changes.

summary: A folder's URL (/guide/ or /guide) is a 404: only /guide/index.html works
detail: Noted 19 Sep 2026 writing the skill: the site route maps a path to <path>.md, so /guide/ looks for 'guide/.md' and /guide for 'guide.md'. Serve the folder's index.md for both, the way / already serves index.md; the nav could then link folders as /guide/.
note: 2026-09-19: site.ts resolves a folder to its index.md — /blog, /blog/ and /blog/index.html all serve the same page. Wiki links and the nav still emit index.html, so nothing else changed.

summary: A page whose first line reads like 'Update: closed Monday' loses it to the front matter
detail: Found 19 Sep 2026 writing the skill: parseFrontMatter takes any leading 'word: text' lines as metadata, so a page without front matter that opens with such a sentence silently drops it (checked). The skill now warns (start with a heading or a blank line). Options: treat only known keys (title, theme, nav, toc, x-…) as front matter; or require the blank line that ends it; or YAML-style --- fences.
note: 2026-09-19: front matter is now either a --- fence or the known keys (title, theme, nav, toc, layout, description, draft, date, and x-* for your own). 'Update: closed Monday' is a paragraph again. Breaking for anyone who invented their own bare keys — use x- or a fence.

summary: New sites lose the authoring skill: bun create's setup deletes .claude
detail: Noted 19 Sep 2026: setup removes the whole .claude folder, which now holds the duckdown authoring skill (what a Claude session writing the new site's content should read), railroad's skills and launch.json (the preview pane). Decide what a new site keeps: likely skills/duckdown and launch.json; railroad and bun-route only matter to someone changing the editor.
note: 2026-09-19: create/setup.ts now removes only the repo's own scaffolding; a new site keeps .claude/skills/duckdown and launch.json.

summary: The duck logo kept its own black, in every theme, and vanished in dark mode
detail: Peter asked 19 Sep 2026 whether CSS can colour the duck. It was placed with , and an SVG shown that way is a separate document: the page's CSS and variables can't reach inside it, and currentColor means the file's own colour. On the dark theme the black duck was invisible.
note: 19 Sep 2026: the page now has an empty and the theme paints it: background: var(--duck, currentColor) with the SVG as a -webkit-mask/mask (contain, centred); the eye and wing are holes, so the page still shows through. The duckdown theme sets --duck: var(--accent), so it is teal in light and dark. Two things learned the hard way, both now in the Images guide and the skill: .

summary: Pages written as files don't reach the nav until an editor save or a restart
detail: Seen 19 Sep 2026 adding a blog with the authoring skill: the post rendered at once, but Blog only joined the nav after saving the page in the editor (the cache is dropped by the editor's writes, todo 22). That's fine for the editor, but anyone — or any Claude session — writing pages as files meets it every time. Options: don't cache when DEBUG=1; or check the newest mtime under pages/ (local storage only, an extra stat per request); or leave it, since the skill and CLAUDE.md both say so.
note: 19 Sep 2026: Peter chose the development exception. siteNav(pages, debug = DEBUG) builds per request when DEBUG is on and caches otherwise; navChanged() still drops it in production. Checked on the running dev server: a folder's index.md written straight to disk joined the nav immediately, and left it when deleted, with no editor save. The skill, CLAUDE.md and the CHANGELOG now say so; a unit test covers both ways.

summary: {{pages}} expanded inside code, so no page could show the tag
detail: The listing was substituted across the whole rendered page, including <code> spans and fenced blocks. The guide page documenting {{pages}} had the guide's own folder listing injected into its code sample and its inline code, so the one page that must show the syntax couldn't. Found while checking the seed site for stale docs.
note:
2026-09-19: outsideCode() in utils.ts splits the rendered HTML on ... and substitutes only between the pieces — a fence renders as 
, so one rule covers both. Code is literal, which is what writers expect. The other placeholders were never at risk: {{content}} is substituted last, so a page's text is inserted after they're consumed.

summary: No /health route for a platform healthcheck
detail: Railway (and any platform) wants a cheap endpoint that proves the process is up without depending on content. Today the shallowest check is / , which renders index.md through storage — on S3 that's a network round trip per probe, and a content mistake reads as a dead service.
note: 2026-09-20: /health in main.ts — a static Response, so the probe never touches storage.

summary: A pid file on a persistent volume can permanently block startup in a container
detail: claimPidFile() refuses to start when the pid file names a live process, checking only isAlive(). In a container the app is a low pid (often 1). After a hard restart (SIGKILL, OOM, platform recycle) the file survives on the volume naming pid 1, which is always alive — so the new process throws and the service never starts again: a crash loop with no bad input. stopServer() already has isDuckie() (ps, command line names main.ts); claimPidFile doesn't use it.
note: 2026-09-20: claimPidFile refuses only a live *duckdown* (heldByDuckie = isAlive && isDuckie, the check stopServer already used), and takes the guard as a parameter so both branches are tested deterministically. process.test.ts now runs two real servers for the refusal, and asserts a restart over a recycled pid.

summary: A deployment seeded from the example site ships a public admin/admin
detail: DUCKDOWN_SEED copies tests/example (or create's scaffold) when the content folder is empty, users.json included. That's right for local dev and wrong the moment the site is on the internet: the editor is at a known URL with known credentials. Needs a deliberate answer — an admin password from the environment at seed time, or a refusal to seed default credentials when DEBUG isn't set.
note: 2026-09-20: DUCKDOWN_ADMIN_PASSWORD (with DUCKDOWN_ADMIN_USER, default admin) is written into users.json at startup by ensureAdmin() — the secret lives in the platform, not in git, and changing it changes the password on the next restart. It rewrites only when the password actually changed, so a restart isn't an S3 PUT. Unset, nothing happens, which is every local run.

summary: GitHub reports 36 Dependabot alerts on master; duckdown has five dependencies
detail: The push to master printed 36 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 16 high). All 36 pointed at one manifest, client/package-lock.json — the Vue client, deleted on 2026-03-20 in the rewrite commit. None pointed at package.json or bun.lock, and none of the flagged packages (koa, axios, lodash, postcss, prismjs, minimist, loader-utils, node-forge…) is in the current tree, which is railroad, lucide-static and three dev dependencies. GitHub had not closed them when the manifest went.
note: 2026-09-21: checked against the alert API rather than guessed, then dismissed all 36 as not_used with the reason recorded on each. 0 open now. Left alone, a security page showing 36 alerts and 2 criticals teaches you to ignore it, and a real one in bun.lock would be lost in the noise.

summary: bun create leaves a half-scaffolded site: the postinstall hook doesn't run setup
detail: `bun create blueshed/duckdown x` prints `$ bun run create/setup.ts` and never runs it. Proved it's Bun 1.4.2, not the script: a bun-create.postinstall of `echo HELLO` prints its own command line and produces no output, and `sh -c 'echo > ran.txt'` writes no file anywhere. Bun does read the field — it strips it from the package.json it writes — it just doesn't execute it. The symptom is worse than first logged: without setup there is no .env, so DEBUG isn't set, so the server refuses to start over a missing COOKIE_SECRET — a message that says nothing about the real cause.
note: 2026-09-20: can't be fixed by changing the command, so duckdown stops depending on the hook. server/scaffold.ts spots a copy `bun create` left un-set-up (bun strips the bun-create key, so its absence plus a missing site/ and a present create/setup.ts is the signature) and the COOKIE_SECRET error carries the explanation and the one command that fixes it: bun run setup. Not auto-run: setup deletes tests/ and create/, and doing that silently because someone typed `bun dev` would be worse than the bug. Verified end to end on a faithful copy.

summary: DUCKDOWN_SEED fills a local folder but never a bucket, so an S3 deployment starts empty
detail: seedLocalSite() returns immediately when IS_S3 (`if (s3 || !seed || existsSync(target)) return`). With DUCKDOWN_BUCKET set, a fresh deployment therefore has no pages, no template and no users.json — the site 404s and nobody can sign in, with nothing in the logs to say why. There is no supported way to get a scaffolded site/ into a bucket; blueshed.co.uk needed a hand-written upload script (scripts/seed-bucket.ts there). The fix mirrors the local path: when the bucket has no pages/index.md, copy the seed folder up, then say so in the startup banner. Guard it the same way — seed only when the target is empty — so it can never overwrite a live site.
note: 2026-09-20: seedBucketSite() in storage.ts uploads DUCKDOWN_SEED when the bucket holds no pages/index.md, called from main.ts after seedLocalSite(). Guarded like the local path — only into an empty site, so it can never overwrite one being written — and it says in the log what it did, or that the seed folder wasn't there. Tested against the fake S3.

summary: A placeholder used twice in a template was only filled once
detail: The template was filled with .replace("{{title}}", fn), and String.replace with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. blueshed.co.uk's template used {{title}} in <title> and again in og:title, so every page published <meta property="og:title" content="{{title}}"> — the placeholder itself, on the live site.
note: 2026-09-20: fill() uses a global regex per placeholder, so a template may use one anywhere and as often as it likes; {{content}} is still filled last so a page's own text is never scanned. Found by checking the deployed page's meta tags.

summary: templates/ and static/ can't be edited, so a deployed site's template can only be changed out of band
detail: The editor reaches pages/ (and images through /edit/browse). templates/site.html, static/site.css and anything else under static/ are not editable. On a local site that's fine — edit the files. On a bucket-backed deployment the bucket is the only copy and is never re-seeded, so changing the template means writing to S3 by hand; blueshed.co.uk needed a script for it. Either let the editor open templates/ and static/ text files, or give duckdown a documented way to push them.
note: 2026-09-20: the editor has sections. fileRoutes(prefix, store, changed) in routes/files.ts is the file API over one folder; pages/, templates/ and static/ each get their own route rooted in their own folder, so none can reach across them and users.json (hashes, at the site root) is in none of them. The browser has pages | templates | static, and switching puts down whatever was open so a file can't be saved into the wrong folder. A template is neither markdown nor CSS, so the preview says so instead of rendering its placeholders as prose.

summary: Three URLs serve each page and each claims itself canonical
detail: Since folders are served by their index, /journey, /journey/ and /journey/index.html all answer 200. {{url}} reports whichever was asked for, so each is canonical for itself — duplicate content, three ways. The nav and wiki links both emit /index.html, which is the least tidy of the three. Pick one form: have the nav and wiki links emit the folder path, and have {{url}} normalise (drop a trailing index.html, keep one trailing-slash convention) so the other two point at it.
note: 2026-09-21: canonicalPath() in utils.ts is the one rule — index.md is /, a folder's index is /folder/, anything else is /page.html — and the canonical is computed from the key the request resolved to, not from the address asked for, so all three forms name the same page. The nav and markCurrent use the same rule, so the links crawlers follow are the canonical ones. The seed's template gained the canonical link (only the website's had it), the seed's own links were canonicalised, and the guide and reference say which of the three is the real address.

summary: layout: had no user anywhere, and the seed shipped a broken Tornado template
detail: Nothing in tests/example, .dev-site or blueshed.co.uk used layout:, so a feature with tests had never been used in practice. Worse, the seed shipped templates/site_tmpl.html — {{ handler.one_meta_value('title') }}, {% end %} — the Python duckdown's Tornado template. Nothing referenced it, it would render its own tags as text if anything did, and it appeared in the editor's template list looking like a real choice.
note: 2026-09-21: site_tmpl.html removed; templates/post.html added with a dated post in a new seed blog that uses it. {{date}} added so a template can show a page's date, sharing dateHtml() with the folder listings. Two test fixtures were quietly fighting over the name templates/post.html — the older layout test created and deleted it — which is why the new one failed only when the whole suite ran.

summary: dateHtml shows the previous day west of UTC
detail: new Date("2026-09-21") parses as UTC midnight but the Intl.DateTimeFormat formats in the server's local timezone: with TZ=America/New_York the seed post renders "20 September 2026" under datetime="2026-09-21", and the new server test (which expects 21 September) fails on such a machine. Passes on a UTC host, so deployment hides it. Pre-existing in the listings; moved into utils.ts unchanged. Fix: add timeZone: "UTC" to the formatter.
note: 2026-09-21: Intl.DateTimeFormat now takes timeZone: "UTC". A date: has no time in it, so it is a label, not a moment — it must read the same wherever the server runs. Proved by running the whole suite under TZ=America/New_York, and units.test.ts now asserts dateHtml directly.

summary: setup.ts carries a second copy of templates/site.html
detail: The scaffolder writes its own inline template, so e620f1a had to add the canonical link in two places and the two will drift again. Copy tests/example/templates/site.html as setup.ts already does for static/site.css.
note: 2026-09-21: setup.ts copies tests/example/templates/site.html, as it already did for static/site.css. The inline copy was byte-identical, so nothing changed but the number of places to edit.

summary: The plain-word guard is written twice, and template() is roundabout
detail: /^[\w-]+$/ guards both layout (line 39) and css (line 105): it is the path-traversal guard, so one plainName() helper keeps the two from diverging. template() could be names = plain(layout) ? [layout, "site"] : ["site"] instead of a loop with a continue. The inner name in renderPage's fill loop also shadows the outer name.
note: 2026-09-21: plainName() in the new page.ts guards both layout: and css:. templateFor() is a list, not a loop with a continue, and returns which template it settled on. The shadowed name went with the move.

summary: post.html prints a dangling "Posted " for a post with no date:
detail: {{date}} correctly returns nothing, but the label around it is fixed. The seed is the model users copy: show the label only with a date, or drop it.
note: 2026-09-21: the template writes {{date}} alone; site.css puts the label in .posted::before and hides .posted:empty, so a post with no date leaves nothing behind.

summary: css: has no user; layout: and theme: already cover its ground (YAGNI)
detail: No page in tests/example or .dev-site says css:, as layout: had none until #54. theme: is a few variables, layout: is the whole shape; css: sits between them, and reference.md's three sizes of override could be two. Drop it, or hold it until something needs it (check blueshed.co.uk first).
note: 2026-09-21: it has a user now — tests/example/pages/blog/one-page-that-looks-different.md, the css: demo. blueshed.co.uk doesn't use it, but the seed does, and the seed is what teaches it. Keeping it.

summary: CLAUDE.md describes utils.ts as wildcard path extraction only
detail: utils.ts now also holds escapeHtml, outsideCode, canonicalPath and dateHtml. Also reference.md has a double blank line before "Three sizes of override".
note: 2026-09-21: CLAUDE.md lists page.ts and describes utils.ts by what is in it; the site/mark section now describes the shared renderer. The double blank line in reference.md is gone.

summary: The preview builds its own shell, so editing a template changes nothing in it
detail: A resource pane can now open templates/site.html beneath the page, but the preview never sees it: Preview.tsx wraps the rendered markdown in a shell of its own making, so a draft template body has nowhere to go and {{nav}} is missing from the preview entirely. /edit/mark/ should render the whole document through the real template, taking an optional draft template body in the request, and Preview should send the open resource's draft when it is the template the page uses.
note: 2026-09-21: server/page.ts holds parsePage() and pageHtml(); routes/site.ts and routes/mark.ts both go through it, so the preview is the real document — template, nav, {{pages}}, theme cascade. PUT /edit/mark/ takes JSON ({source, draft}) and answers {html, layout, meta}. An unsaved template is used when it is the one the page wears; a stylesheet still goes straight into the head with no round trip.

summary: Nothing says when the open template isn't the one the page uses
detail: Opening templates/post.html while looking at a page whose layout: is site.html edits something the preview will never show. The pane had a line saying so; the PaneHeader refactor dropped it and it was not put back. Say it once, in the pane, without blocking the edit — you may well be editing the template you are about to switch to.
note: 2026-09-21: pageHtml() reports the template it used, the preview puts it in pageLayout, and ResourcePane says "The page you are looking at uses site.html" when you have another template open. It says it once and edits anyway.
